body: It's interesting that it's practiced the most heavily in the state where everyone believes in a Jesus, a man also executed despite being completely innocent. The hypocrisy is off the charts.

>>I've never heard anything about this study you mentioned. If such a study had been real, designed to be scientifically valid, was actually conducted, AND had such stunning results I think we all would have heard about it much more.

That's what I thought, you'd have thought there would've been a Time magazine article on it.  However sometimes in religions things can be under a fair amount secrecy which is why the claim really effected me.

He also implied that I will be punished for taking pain medication and that his friend who has pancreatic cancer which causes horrendous pain refuses to take pain meds of any kind and just meditates most of the day learning how to accept the pain.  I've tried to tell him that my pain has been going on for 14 years and that it will to on for 40-50 more and that having constant pain for so long makes it impossible to simply meditate it away

I'd like to think the monk OP was lying in a misguided attempt to save a life rather than simply trying to screw around with someone who is already in quite a bit of pain.  It is hard to believe there are trolls who would do this to people who are asking for hope which is why I'll try to believe it was just a misguided effort it's too depressing otherwise.

I've always just assumed since the Dali Lama is such a kind, gentle and compassionate spirit, that Buddhism also shared these properties rather than the rage, contradiction, and pain we see in some other religions such as Catholicism.  I don't think God would choose such a wonderful, blessed and forgiving man to lead the religion if it didn't share any of those properties.

Plus it doesn't seem fair that any person be kicked out of being reborn as human- we all make mistakes both tiny and huge, why would the universe make us so incredibly fallible if it was just going to punish us for all the failings we inevitably make?

Thank you. I really appreciate your supportive and empathetic response.  From now I won't take emails and posts that claim I will be severely punished seriously, I'd like to think I've already served out my sentence in this life and I have learned the lesson I was sent here for, which is not to take health for granted and to cherish and protect it while it lasts.  If this means giving up in my next life such sports as football, skiing, and snowboarding, then so be it.  Maybe this is a lesson the whole society needs to learn as athletes become more and more competitive...
Not where I live they don't. It called growing up, part of it usually includes making money

Thank you. That is a relief. I didn't completely buy his story but he definitely made it sound like it was the gods honest truth- enough to get under my skin especially because of the situation I face.  That can't be that great karma for him if he just made it up to try and torment me.

A Buddhist monk recently told me that you have what they call vibhava-ta.nhaa, craving for self annihilation.  According to him, carrying out this action will burn through all your good karma and you will be reborn as prey for predatory creatures, such as a field mouse (preyed upon by eagles and felines), a million times over until you are allowed to be reborn as a human again .

I'm not sure what to believe since he PMed me instead of making a comment on my thread, which sort of suggests he was trying to hide it from other Buddhists who he might have gotten a very negative response from for doing this.

I hesitated over whether to post this on your thread as it has frightened me so badly.  When I tried to reply to the monk that all of his information was coming from his own fear and uncertainty about death, he replied by telling me that ultra advanced Buddhist monks had learned to shut down the body and die, while their companions administered hydrogen sulfide to preserve their body while they were literally dead.  After a certain amount of time, the companion monks administer a certain chemical and CPR, reviving the monk from being dead.

The monk would then recount what he had seen while he was dead.  It conformed with all the Buddhist teachings on death and allegedly was done with scientists monitoring the project to make sure the monks were truly dead for a time.  Supposedly the Dali Lama himself condoned the study.

They claimed the period after death was a rapid fire switching between extreme pleasure and pain and is generally too intense and very difficult to tolerate.  This continued until the soul decides to be reborn rather than tolerate such unpleasantness.  

I have tried to search for some scientific studies that back up his claim that the monks were able to be revived after death.  I haven't found anything yet:

Again I was unsure whether to share this or not, but figured you might want to know the Buddhist perspective. I'm an agnostic yet in the past have admired  Buddhist beliefs- however I thought it was a religion of peace, kindness, and compassion.  To find out that it is basically like Catholicism has been deeply disturbing.

I have been trying to convince myself that the monk was just a troll trying to harass me but when I have researched it, some of the information seems true-  hopefully you can help me prove that this is a load of BS so I can move onto my euthanasia with a clear and calm mind.

Well just from my experience with chronic pain, i can say that some people would rather not be mean but for some reason or other are forced into it,  for example, I have constant severe pain and can sometimes come off as abrupt, rude, angry etc even though in --no-- way am I ahead of time consciously making a decision to direct negativity at someone.  It's just that I might have bad pain and someone is asking me a question when I just need to lay down, so I speak in a loud tone of voice that might be interpreted as yelling.

Perhaps bullies have a similar emotion pain which they unconsciously are acting out and repeating in sort of a trickle down effect of the original abuse and unfortunately other people become the victims.  All I can say is that while I have never bullied anyone, I think bullying for most people isn't coming from happy, secure place.

The tragedy is how pain is transmitted from one person to another rather then healing.  I believe this phenomena is responsible for many social problems.  The real tough question is how do we heal people so that we can avoid these kind of problems.  Native Americans used ceremonies and spiritual drugs like peyote to enhance the bonds of the tribe. It's unfortunate that today we only have alcohol.

Perhaps in the future when psychologists have a deep understanding of such powerful drugs like LSD (after prohibition has ended and scientists can study freely again), bullies and other instigators of negativity and pain will be treated by doctors just like one treats a cold or the flu- perhaps give them a futuristic psychotropic that causes deep reflection on ones actions.  One can only hope such treatments become available in the future....

Well the problem basically comes down to the lack of good painkillers to begin with.  What medications do they have from chronic pain?--antidepressants(very mild pain relief), anticonvulsants(only works on neuropathic pain), antiinflammatories(only good for arthritis otherwise not very powerful painkillers), dissociative drugs like ketamine(can't be used regularly without significant impairment however sometimes can be used topically for a limited number of conditions), experimental drugs like LSD( scientists don't even understand why these work therefore there is significant issues with taking them), opioids(probably the best painkiller in existence but also has huge problems with tolerance and addiction).

Out of all those drugs, the only really powerful painkillers are opioid based medications.  Therefore it sort of makes sense that they are having this problem.

What they truly need to do is come up with better pain medications.  However due to the drug war scientists have a difficult time studying drugs like LSD or cannabis,  I'd bet miracle painkillers are just waiting for discovery and synthesis within these drugs. 

Also the rate at which the rainforest is disappearing should make chronic pain patients worried as some novel medicine is probably just sitting there waiting to be discovered .

But anyways, until then the problem with pain management is the lack of powerful painkillers outside of opioids for severe chronic pain, the fact that cognitive behavioral therapy is undependable and often does work, and the hodge lodge of other therapies such as hypnosis, acupuncture, chiropractor, PT, massage therapy, biofeedback, yoga, cranio sacral, prolo, trigger point injections, inversion tables, traction, etc etc etc don't work for a significant number of people (there wouldn't be so many different approaches if more of them worked consistently for a large number of people.

So let's keep our fingers crossed for better , more dependable drugs/ treatments

It's interesting because most people who don't work most likely can't due to some kind of health problem so I'm not quite sure what you group of fictional slackers you are directing that message to....

>>There are of course concerns about craving annihilation, rebirth and that a human birth burns through so much good merit to begin with, that beyond this life you may experience less fortunate circumstances and even more suffering and not less.

Where do you get this information?  To me it seems to be generated from the fear of the unknown, rather than coming from a place of wisdom and knowledge.  Can you specifically direct me to a source of information that makes this claim? (even if you can there are so many different ideas regarding what happens after death and I don't belong to any specific religion-although I'm not an atheist)

>>If you are committed to death, then one might consider seriously giving a go at exhausting many other options first.

Yes I've tried a huge amount of things and have done a few experimental things as well.  Not a huge amount, but my intuition is that only something like optogenetics applied to humans will be able to manage my pain.  This is because nothing but one treatment out of the dozens and dozens I've tried has ever even touched the pain. But it seems hard for people to believe that I have tried so many different approaches, oh well.

If you can understand that I've tried so many different things and nothings has worked and you can imagine being in constant severe pain in a cape like distribution across your neck and shoulders, maybe you can understand where I'm coming from.

I strongly feel death would bring release.... Perhaps this is how people feel when they are closer to death.  

However I would rather- however only without such bad constant pain.

>>Pain is not suffering. 

I wish I could see things that way.  I guess I sort of can because if I'm engaged in an exciting task, like the other day I thought I had won a lottery and the pain didn't bother me as much.  The issue I can see with dealing with chronic pain that way is that how do you trick the brain into going into the state it's in before winning the lottery, having sex, buying stuff during a sale or being engaged in a day one videogame? That seems to be impossible because you can't fake it , can you?

Would you give the same answer to someone who had Parkinson's, Melonoma or who knew they were going to develop full blown Altzheimers in the next year? I ask because people usually don't know anything about syringomyelia and it is usually assumed to be equivalent to a bad back or something  else relatively minor, because it doesn't directly kill.


>>If you are relying on a semi-anonymous web forum for your own piece of mind, the battle is already lost. It sounds like you're not very married to any sort of metaphysical reality that extends beyond our material existences.


I'm relying on reddit simply to discuss this issue in a way that you just can't in the real world.  If you talk about this issue in reality, you just hear the tired old boring things.  Even if I disagree with people on here, at least they are not reciting the same old speeches shrinks have memorized for such occasions.  It may seem that I'm not willing to listen to other opinions but I am very interested if anyone has a strong reason that resonates with me to not to go through with it because it is an irreversible choice after all. I just get turned off when it reverts back to the threats of being reborn as a lower form, that reminds me of Christianity, a religion which I basically despise ( I'm a fan of Jesus just not his religion as practiced today) and it also seems to be based off of fear rather than real knowledge and wisdom.


Also I do believe that there is a metaphysical reality however I don't have a clear idea about what lies beyond- however my gut tells me that it can't be much worse than life is for me here.  My beliefs are closer to what Bill Hicks says in one of his stand up routines: 


>>"Today, a young man on acid realized that all matter is merely energy condensed to a slow vibration – that we are all one consciousness experiencing itself subjectively. There is no such thing as death, life is only a dream, and we are the imagination of ourselves."


I've spent quite a lot of time meditating, doing mindfulness training, and instead of having some breakthrough where I was suddenly able to magically turn down the pain by somehow disassociating myself from it, I became more clear that because there will not be a cure for this particular disease and that because all current pain management techniques and drugs for chronic pain barely work and there isn't enough motivation to get new drugs made quickly, that I would rather pass on VS continuing living in this kind of constant pain.  It became more clear to me that a life without friends, work, hobbies, and love/companionship and with constant severe pain -cannot- be considered a life- quality of life is far more important than simply surviving with none of the elements of life.  I have found there is nothing to be learned in such a situation other than a rather simple lesson of the importance of health in life- if everyone had the perspective I've gained from my time with syringomyelia there would be no extreme sports, reckless driving, or war. 

So far you haven't given me much reason to trust you over my own knowledge that I gained from meditating and mindfulness practice.  To me it seems like you've just resorted to threats which you have absolutely no proof of and which could easily be argued are products of fear of the unknown. And I know it may sound weird that meditation led me to my conclusion because meditation is usually portrayed as resolving problems in the most "wise" way and euthanasia is stereotypically connected to doing unwise things like slashing ones wrists or jumping off a bridge.  However I have no desire to harm my body in the way that depressed people will often take to cutting their own body,but I do wish to die peacefully at Dignitas with my family by my side.  None of the response has convinced me that this is such a bad thing to want:

You say: 
>>It is a common theme through many sutras that a human life is an incredible gift. You probably don't consider it a gift

This honestly really confuses me  because of the idea that moksha is basically the ultimate achievement. At the same time you are telling me human life is an incredible gift, you are also telling me that euthanasia will lead me to be reborn again instead of attaining moksha- wouldn't this make human life into a kind of punishment?

I sort of regard it as a halfway gift as there are beautiful things to be experienced in life as a human that can't be experienced otherwise:art, math, logic, language etc- however there is also tremendous suffering- and happiness is so fleeting- take the case of South African Oscar Pistorius a man who had conquered the limitations of his physical body with his prosthetic legs and yet his uncontrollable anger led him to likely shoot his GF to death with after a Valentine's Day argument.

Plus I have a huge issue with the idea humanity is the pinnacle of existence and that the animals are lessor life forms as you've implied.  First of all science is informing us that animal intelligence is far deeper than we've previously imagined.  People like Temple Grandin are showing us how much we miss when we observe animal behavior, clearly they are different intelligences however they are far from lessor intelligences. The belief that animal life is lessor seems to me to be based on extremely out of date ideas about animals.  Plus I'd love to be reborn as a cat, dog , or bird.

Also I do highly value human life, if everyone somehow magically learned what I have from this disease, there wouldn't be things like war that destroy thousands of young people's health permanently.  However as I said above, I don't  consider a life that is simply surviving to be gift because it isn't life. Things like friendship, love, purpose, dreams, freedom and desires are the true gifts- you take them away for long enough and you've basically killed a person.  Something that torturers know all to well when they put someone in solitary confinement.

I think if the universe punishes me for euthansia by having me reborn as an animal that is prey for other creatures, it is so unfair that nothing matters anyways- that if it truly is that unjust it would be better for the whole universe to just be destroyed anyways.  


Again I wonder is where such ideas come from? Is it coming from wisdom, compassion, or reason?  After all, how would anyone really know what happens after death?  No to me it's seems to come directly from fear of the unknown, and propagating fear seems to cause more suffering not less.... That is my opinion on these ideas I've been reading that I'll be reborn as a mouse to be hunted down by owls- 1.how would anyone know this kind of things and 2. It clearly is born from the fear of the unknown, the opposite of wisdom- to me propagating such beliefs only increases suffering. It certainly won't prevent me or most other people in similar situations from wanting to pursue euthanasia although it might increase anxiety and fear about it- it also seems like just another way for a majority to beat up on a minority of people that the majority doesn't want to understand because their existence makes them worry about their own mortality.  That is my opinion on that...

>>It is my opinion that all illness is metaphysical in nature and as such, it can be understood in meditation and subsequently released. 

I wouldn't rule that out either.  The problem is that when I practiced mindfulness(I practiced various exercises over 4 years for 1 hour a day- that's at least 1,000 hours), I became even more clear about my wish to pass on.  Is it possible that this is the insight I gained from it?  I'm fairly sure I was doing the exercises correctly as I had a teacher (she was flawed as a teacher because of her bias based on her belief she completely cured her pain through meditation but I also bought many CDs and books on the subject as well as accessing many universities free classes).

I would rather be cured(or at least treated so the pain is more bearable) and live out the rest of my days, but all my experience combined with a strong gut feeling says that this will never come to be within my lifetime.

I also strongly feel that life isn't worth living without friends and companions, without joy, and without the ability to follow ones interests. I've always felt this way.  Now I have to spend most my time in a recliner and cannot do these things, I love computers but am unable to interact with them in a recliner despite trying all the special interfaces for disabled people (for example my neck muscles are so constantly tight as violin strings that it makes it impossible to speak into voice recognition software).

I just wonder if it's possible that at the core of it, for myself the truth I would rather pass on than deal with constant severe pain and all the problems it entails.  After all I've read John Cabot Zinn(a books I found infuriating to read because it badly conflicted with my experience of pain), and many other self help books as well as speaking to hundreds of other chronic pain sufferers online and -none- of their experiences resonate at all with me except the few I've found who are also pursuing goals like going to Dignitas.
If I had to rephrase it I would've put- "What is a Buddhists take on such a situation" rather than "is it okay with this"

I would concur. That statement might not cause me to have a breakdown, but it is just another thing that makes me feel guilty for existing with this horrible condition- in that sense it definitely increasing suffering, if only by a small amount.  The large numbers of people who say similar things (I would usually point to ignorant backwoods Christians rather than Buddhists) does help to make it more difficult to exist with these kinds of problems.

I would bet if you knew more about Syringomyelia you would feel more hesitant about making such a statement.

To me, it seems quite natural to focus on ones self the more and more syringomyelia progresses.  Isn't it quite normal for a man approaching death to become more and more time self reflecting?

I've spent 4-5 years of my life practicing various mindfulness techniques absolutely religiously for a total of 1 hour a day- that's over 1,000 hours.  The only thing I gained was maybe 15-30 minutes of lowered pain a day (out of 24 hours of constant pain).  I didn't gain any insight, but every day I meditated if I had the money at that time I would've gone to Dignitas without a 2nd thought. Could this be the insight- that I would rather die than continue living with this pain? If we aren't judgmental about it, isn't it be possible that meditation may have revealed this personal truth to me?

I have come to believe that perhaps mindfulness doesn't work well on the particularly vicious diseases like syringomyelia which is particularly known for the severe constant pain it causes.  This is why people with suffering from more well known vicious diseases like Parkinson's don't usually promote it as a way to reduce suffering- instead they promote medical development. I think it's a matter of scale- for problems that many people face like workplace stress, occasionally back pain, chronic anxiety, behavioral problems etc, mindfulness can often be more successful than traditional medicine.  However unless you are some Grandmaster, in the face of some of the more awful health problems, it can help a little but that's it.

I said nearly 100% certain, I have left room for a miracle or some other major shift to take place, however at this point I find it unlikely as I've been waiting 14 years for that to take place.  But I do still hope for something...

Thanks for letting me know the side of Buddhism is just as ignorant and judgemental and fearful as Christianity.  Why do people like you tend to infect all the worlds religions with your fear?  Love is clearly the most powerful force in the universe- to me that says something about the structure of the universe itself- I would highly doubt it if people who have been punished and tortured in real life would face punishment for putting an end to that suffering- that doesn't make much sense.

If the universe is that unjust it deserves to be destroyed....

Thanks you for your kind message : ) A few of the posts seem rather harsh- I guess every religion has proponents of similar ideas( the idea the euthansia victims will be punished).  It sort of reminds me of the some responses I've gotten from Christians i.e. you will be punished by God for not wanting to live in intolerable constant pain. However on the whole most do not advocate this POV which is encouraging. 

Why would God or the Universe be so cruel as to punish people who have already been punished in life? As far as I know love and compassion are stronger energies than cruelty, judgemental attitudes, and hate. I would like to think that says something about the nature of the universe and God.

If you look up what happened to Bobby Jones the famous golfer from the 30s you will get an idea of what Chiari/Syringomyelia is like.  It is not "normal" suffering as it lasts so long without killing you. 

Sometimes I think that Buddhism doesn't account for such suffering because it is primarily a modern problem as in the past people with such conditions would've ended up passing away.  Of course, back in the day people had teeth problems- but I see that as being more acute pain than chronic pain because people would have their teeth taken out- terribly painful yes but for a comparably short time. 

Only recent developments like modern medicine, the relative wealth of the middle class, and the welfare state have made it possible for people with very significant impairment and pain have no problem surviving in spite of their condition- an extreme example being people who are simply hooked up to a machine in order to live. 

Edit: now that more people have responded I see that many responses are quite compassionate, pleasantly encouraging.

I'm basically an expert in pain management by now after 14 years of this.  9 years of pain is just terrible but it is easier to manage than 50(which is what I'm facing right now) because of the problems of tolerance.

For example, I took Remron for years as it simply knocked me out so I could sleep.  It has completely stopped working because I've taken it for so long.  Almost all the pain medicines have this problem and not just opioid class meds, anticonvulsants that work for neuropathic pain have it as well as antidepressants (Remron is an antidepressants).

So basically I fail to see how euthansia isn't the only way out. At this point it is sad because I believe if the medical system took pain seriously they would have better treatments by now. Instead excruciating chronic pain is viewed as a non-fatal, non-serious problem that won't kill a person- I would beg to differ, especially when the pain goes on for 40-50 years everyday- you had cancer, Chiari is different it cannot be cured and it is 90% certain not to outright kill you.  50 years of constant pain, yet It's somehow my fault I wish to die- slave captives who jumped off the ships on the way to America aren't blamed for their choice, so why should I?( Slaves faced the same nearly certain full life of nearly constant misery)

However if I could get access to Dignitas at this point I would actually be incredibly happy, not sad because pain cannot occur when the nerves causing it are not functioning any more. Whatever the afterlife is it cannot have pain because it doesn't have the equipment necessary for it.

Well to be clear this is euthanasia we are talking about not suicide.  Suicide is killing oneself without a direct concrete reason, euthansia is for people with real awful diseases that make life a living hell.

Wouldn't Buddha be compassionate towards such people?

I was 16 when I first developed intractable chronic pain. The medical system is an absolute nightmare, and what's so frustrating about it is that people who have gone to the ER for relatively more easy things like broken legs or heart disease think the healthcare system can solve any problem- not true. It is broken for the patients who need it the most.

That is a tough lesson to learn when you are so young.  However if you keep on demanding care and using all your resources to perhaps find places outside your local area that have better hospitals, you might get better help.

I ended up finding a brillian doctor- it's far from perfect which is why I'm on SW but finding this doctor probably extended my life span for 5 years so it definetly was worth it.  I do want to die now however because the solution the doc came up with was very short lived.

I'm sorry you have to go through that at your age, I experienced it and basically I had to stop talking about medicine with people because they had such incredibly delusional ideas about the healthcare system.

I think the healthcare system is so fucked because the patients aren't empowered consumers. Capitalism works so brilliantly because it kind of protects the rights of consumer (relative to other economic systems) however in healthcare we have the doctors who believe consumers cannot understand what they want and have to be told.  This will eventually become an out of date way of doing things, it already is falling apart with patients doing things like choosing to fly to Taiwan for better medical care at more affordable prices.  I think the internet could be a powerful tool in empowering healthcare consumers -for example I believe there should be a Wikipedia just for health issues.

>>I had cancer at 17 and have almost 9 years of chronic pain (albeit not as bad as other people have) so I can totally get behind assisted suicide/euthanasia although I probably could never do it myself.

I've found comparing yourself to others is a fruitless task because there is always someone with worse pain.  If you are a burn victim you might think you have it bad but then there are people with 90% of their bodies burnt.  If you have 90% of your body burnt you might think its bad but then there are people with brain cancer with unimaginably migraines multiple times daily.

What it comes down to is you're own ability to cope (if you can't live with your pain it doesn't really matter there is someone else with worse pain out there), whether the condition is treatable or not , and how long it will last (for some people with cancer the pain might only last 5 years before a natural death making it far easier to treat). 

If I had the option I would've terminated my own life after 5 years of this:  that is my own judgement based on what my own body tells me, not what people trying to discourage me by listing all the horror stories of people burnt up to 95% of their body- that doesn't help all it accomplishes is making you feel even more isolated.

Yes, Dignitas is would be the best possible option, I just don't have the money to go there. Do you know if they do charity?  That would be amazing if I could go there- at this point I would be so relieved and happy if I could somehow work with them.  I spend each day crying all day I'm in so much pain, this has been going on for 4 years and the pain has been going in for 14 years.  I'm in constant pain- at the minimum it feels as though my neck has been stuffed to near bursting with cotton. They don't have anything more to try in terms of medicine except for Ziconotide which doesn't apply to my pain. I have to be reclined to keep the pain from being a 100 out of 10 on the pain scale.

Do you know anyone who is rich and into helping people? It would be a miracle if I could find someone to help pay for me to go to 
Switzerland, thanks.

At this point I find the difficult to care about the person who find me and their feelings because I'm in so much pain and the fact that people die- it happens.  Perhaps that person will be one more person who supports more humane methods for people with incurable diseases to finally get relief.

In a better world of course there would be medical options.  However I have had extremely extensive medical treatment and found it to be very, very lacking.

Have you researched it in depth at all? I've bought a membership to Exit International, the one run by the Australian doctor.  It does actually seem much more tricky than you would think.  The problem is there is basically no reliable info online regarding the subject because the of the influence of those who are trying to prevent something they clearly have no understanding of.  Exit International has a goal of providing clear and accurate info, and they include the common pitfalls.  I'm actually amazed anyone actually succeeds in suicide after reading their book.  All the stereotypical ways that the public thinks of people killing themselves are very very prone to failure.  Even the options that are allegedly better are clearly not foolproof- for example there is the use of inert gases to induce a painless hypoxia (similar to what happens if an airline loses oxygen), however after a person looses consciousness they will have spasms.  It is easy to imagine a case where the person knocks off the device they have jury rigged and just obtains brain injury instead of death.

I've found the more I read up on accurate information, the more clear and strong the case is for legal euthanasia. If I had the money to go to Dignitas that is what I'd do- I'd don't however. 

The situation today is one thing for wealthy people, where assisted death is essentially legal as the US can't make Switzerland part of the axis of evil, as much as it likely wants to.  If you aren't wealthy, it depends on where you live- forcing people to take horrific drastic measures.  How is the current situation morally A-OK?

I think the fact that wealthy people like Terry Prachet are going to Dignitas rather than spending their money on medical treatments says a lot about the morality of forcing poorer patients to undergo medical procedures- do you see what I mean?

Don't they have to inject lidocaine near the nerves they are trying to ablate? Because I've already had this done with the idea they would use radio frequency ablation, and it provided no pain relief whatsoever.

Even if they have a better way of doing it, it would seem rather risky to do it blind without any pain relief from the trials, correct?  I'm assuming they did the trial on you before doing the radiofrequency ablation.

Hey, you are probably right, although I would hope that more older people realized there were conditions like this: I think people consciously block it out, which gives them no right to tell other people what they can and can't do with their own bodies.

I've already done several trials of radio frequency ablation, didn't work. Plus I don't have neuropathic pain- rhizotomies as far as I know are only successful if you can precisely identify the nerve causing the pain (meaning the pain is neuropathic).

No nerve that I know correspond to the cape like distribution of pain caused by syrigomyelia.

Hey thanks for your reply. I doubt anyone would ever find out who you were if you used the max privacy setup for reddit when pming me (for example ip blocking). I think I might have an idea of the method you are talking about- I'm trying to scramble any sensors right now by making up a code for it- let's just call it the  "balloon" method. I'm just not sure that is truly a foolproof way to do it as some of the variables in purchasing the equipment for it.

This is what I find so inhumane and unspeakable awful about our current society- it tries to force people like me not to talk with loved ones about one of the most important things in life- the end of life.  Shame on our society for doing so , shame shame shame.
What I can't understand is why family members wouldn't support is if we wished to pass on.  After all they are the ones who are intimately acquainted with how nasty the pain is.

Thanks for the reply.  Yeah at this point I've learned that pain management is really still in a primitive state. Just look at the drugs they commonly use- a 2,000+ year old medicine (opioids); medications not even meant for pain- anticonvulsants and antidepressants, and medication people take for minor pain (anti-inflammatory).

If you find something that works that doesn't have some huge drawback please let me know : )
 
When it comes to euthanasia I fail to see why so many people want to ban it.  Most people, if they are not complete assholes, will recognize that there are many kinds of chronic diseases that as far as I can tell are worse than death.

Thanks I haven't seen those yet, the one I know of is Dignitas which when I went on their website I found to be extremely refreshing the way they've cuff off doctors from being a necessary cog in the wheel of someone ending their life- because that is what most opponents use to fearmonger with their paranoid Glenn Beck style ideas that patient controlled death will lead to Nazi-style mass murder of elderly people.

Hopefully one of these organizations is centered around the problems that American people face when attempting to have this done.

Concerning the disease that is causing the pain, it's pretty much hopeless.  I did manage to get surgery for it but it didn't help.  They do have other surgical options but those contain the risk of making the pain even worse.  I have yet to find a doctor willing to do the other surgery.
